Source: Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning, Community Data Snapshots 2026, drawing on American Community Survey 2024 estimates. Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

Why two houses in West Elsdon do not price the same

Windows are the tell on housing this age. A 1956 median means original or early-replacement sash, painted-shut uppers, and storm windows that have been painted over more than once. That is prep work rather than paint work, and it is the line that separates a quote that holds from one that grows. With 3,996 owner households and 1,580 renting, this is two markets in one place: owners doing a room or an elevation at a time, and small landlords wanting a unit turned around cleanly between tenants. They are not the same quote.

What an estimate here has to account for

  • Distance, stated. West Elsdon is 5.6 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to West Elsdon is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.
  • Containment, not just paint. 82.5 percent of housing in West Elsdon was built before 1970, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.
  • Trim, counted separately. At a median of 6 rooms, casing, baseboard and doors are the half of an interior that actually varies. A single number for the whole house hides it.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is postwar brick: bungalow, Cape Cod and the first generation of ranch. Little of the outside takes paint at all, so a West Elsdon exterior is soffit, fascia, overhangs, doors and the garage. Inside it is small rooms with a great deal of casing in them.

It is read off exactly two things: the 1956 median build year, and the split between 67.8 percent detached houses, 2.9 percent attached homes and 28.4 percent in buildings of two units or more.

Inference, and worth saying so. Wall material in West Elsdon is not in the Census tables or the regional data, which is why that sentence carries no number when everything else here does.

West Elsdon is mostly pre-1978 stock, and that changes the setup

82.5 percent of housing units were built before 1970, and the community-area data does not publish a 1978 bucket, so the real pre-1978 share is higher than that by an amount nobody has measured in West Elsdon. That puts most of the housing inside the federal lead-safe renovation rule, which attaches to pre-1978 homes and to work that disturbs the paint on them. In Illinois it is administered by EPA rather than by a state agency.

The practical content of it is dust. Where paint in a West Elsdon room gets disturbed past about six square feet, twenty outside, or wherever a window comes out, the work has to be contained and cleaned to a standard. That is time at both ends of the job, and it is why an honest quote on 3,996 homes worth of 1956-median housing reads longer than a fast one.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in West Elsdon.

Ask about it early. It changes the sequence of a job rather than the price of the paint, and a contractor who has thought about it will tell you in plain terms what happens on day one.

No lead-safe certification is claimed anywhere on this site, because no number has been provided to put here. The panel below leaves the slot open on purpose, in West Elsdon and everywhere else. Ask any contractor for theirs.

Questions

Asked about West Elsdon

Is the $254,623 median home value in West Elsdon what a job here costs?

No. That figure describes the houses, not the work. $254,623 is what the Census estimates a home in West Elsdon is worth, and it earns its place on this page because value tracks size and age, which is what a painter is actually pricing. There is no price list on this site because there is no honest local one to publish yet.

Who actually shows up in West Elsdon?

Mike Walsh owns the company, walks the job and stays on it while our crew works. Call 708-935-4289. It is worth saying because on a job this size the gap between whoever measured it and whoever turns up is where most of the disappointment comes from.

Can it be done a room at a time?

Yes, and on 6-room housing it is often the right call. Doing one room properly beats doing four at a pace that shows, and it spreads the cost across seasons rather than across a credit card. Say that is what you want when you call, because it changes how the work is sequenced.

What changes the price most on a house here?

The state of the trim and the ceilings. Wall area is predictable, and with 6 median rooms and a 1956 median build year in West Elsdon the woodwork is where the hours actually go. Ask for it as its own line and the differences between two quotes stop being mysterious.
